snetwork test · where am I on the network, at a glance

USAGE
  snetwork                       the summary: every section, a few lines each
  snetwork SECTION [ITEM]       one section in full · see snetwork -h sections
  snetwork all                   every section in full

PROBES  plain snetwork sends no packets
  --active[=30s]            also probe: sweep this LAN (a /24 at most), ping the
                         gateway and tailnet peers, time DNS, scan Wi-Fi, ask the
                         internet. Changes nothing. The interval is for --watch.
  --watch[=2s]              redraw every interval and mark changes: green new,
                         yellow older, red gone. The interval needs the "=".

OTHER MACHINES  over ssh; they need snetwork too
  --via HOST             run on HOST and show its answer here
  -no-remote             do not ask tailnet routers about the subnets behind them
                         (full views ask; plain snetwork never does)

OUTPUT
  -json                  the same data as JSON
  -no-color              no colour (also off when output is not a terminal)

OTHER
  -v, -version           print the version
  -h, -help [TOPIC]      this help · topics: sections, env

EXAMPLES
  snetwork --active              # everything, probed; pending values show as …
  snetwork vpn --watch           # tailnet peers, redrawn every 2 s
  snetwork devices 10.0.1.0/24   # asks the tailnet peer that routes that subnet
  snetwork all > network.txt     # everything, no colour

Flags go before or after the section, and -json and --json both work.
